question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw external-content wrappers by default, expose an opt-in captureFilter config option, or wait for the broader provenance architecture?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent fix defines a security boundary and potentially a new public configuration surface.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented excludeWrapped option with schema, manifest, docs, and upgrade-safe default tests.

options.title: Defer to provenance design
options.body: Keep this narrow filter open until the broader memory trust/provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is connected to the external-content wrapper hardening path and is subscribed to this issue's security/product decision surface.
